# x c of one limb, c a power of two

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `mul_pow2_step_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $x c$:

$$z \approx x c.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mul_pow2(x, c, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `T`, `SoAView<T, 1>` | `bool` | the step of the loop the function calls, once per element; not `constexpr`; rounds (loop `mul_pow2_map_1`) |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the functions are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/batch.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include; a view of `T` is taken where the table writes a view of `const T`. They take no marker: a function on arrays compiles only while the kernels of its loop are proved ([Functions on arrays](batch.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $c$ is a power of two: $c = 2^n$ for an integer $n$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z = \mathrm{RN}(x c)$: the number of the format nearest to $x c$, ties to even.
- $\lvert z - x c\rvert \le \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $2^{-1075} \approx 2.4703 \times 10^{-324}$ | $2^{-150} \approx 7.0065 \times 10^{-46}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0.0`, `0x1p-1074` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-149f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0.0`, `0x1p-1074` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-149f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `mul_pow2_step_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/MapSteps.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/MapSteps.v), against `mul_pow2_step_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions mul_pow2_step_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition mul_pow2_step_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x c : R,
  fmt emin prec x ->
  fmt emin prec c ->
  (exists n : Z, c = bpow radix2 n) ->
  let z := mul_pow2_step_1 emin prec tie_even x c in
  fmt emin prec z /\
  z = RN emin prec (x * c) /\
  Rabs (z - (x * c)) <= (1 / 2) * eta emin.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `mul_pow2_step_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** one rounding to nearest of a product by a power of two. **License:** bound: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/mul_pow2_step_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/mul_pow2_step_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The step of the map mul_pow2_map_1, an array of one limb times a power of two: the product
# rounded to nearest, exact but in the underflow range. The program supplies both; a product needs
# no guard (rule R3).

z = prod(x, c)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#mul_pow2_step_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 96 815 808 | 0 | 1 | yes |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 97 117 092 | 0 | 1 | yes |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 274 879 | 0 | 1 (`fp:8:-14:6`) | yes |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
